transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because things have been getting kind of messed up at my job. I'm a waitress, and, um, what really scared everyone at work recently is that I started just... freezing up in the middle of service. 

Or I'll do things completely out of order. Like, the other day, I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually going and closing out the checks. I don't really know why I was doing it, but it really freaked my manager out, so... that's why they wanted me to come see you.
When you were standing at the soda station repeating the table numbers, were you aware of what was happening around you at that moment, or did it feel like you were in some kind of fog or daze?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't think it felt like a fog, exactly. It's just... I don't really remember noticing what was going on around me. I was just focused on saying the numbers. I guess I don't really know how aware I was of the rest of the restaurant right then.
During these episodes when you're repeating the numbers or freezing up, do you completely lose consciousness, or are you aware of what's happening even if you can't control it?

I definitely don't lose consciousness. Like, I don't pass out or fall down or anything like that. I'm awake. But... I don't know if I'd say I'm completely aware of everything, either. 

It's more like my brain is just... stuck on whatever I'm doing right then, like saying the numbers. So I'm awake, and my eyes are open, but I'm just not really taking in anything else around me. I don't really know how to explain it better than that.
How often are these episodes happening? Are we talking about once a week, multiple times a week, or something else?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't been keeping track of exactly how often it happens. I know it's been enough times recently that my manager got really concerned and told me to come here, but... I couldn't tell you if it's exactly once a week or multiple times a week. I just don't really have a specific number for you.
After these episodes end, can you remember everything that happened while you were repeating the numbers or freezing up, or is there a blank spot in your memory for what occurred during that time?

Um... I don't think it's a complete blank spot. Like, I know that I was doing it. I remember saying the numbers. But since I wasn't really noticing anything else while it was happening, I don't have any memory of what was going on around me in the restaurant. So... I guess I remember being stuck, but I just couldn't tell you what else happened during that time.

When these episodes happen where you freeze up or get stuck repeating the numbers, can you think of anything that triggered them? Like, was there something stressful happening at work right before it started, or did it just happen out of the blue?

I've tried to think about that, actually. Um... I don't really think there's a specific trigger. Like, work is always a little busy since it's a restaurant, but it's not like I was having a really stressful moment or dealing with a bad customer right before it happened. 

It really just... it seems to happen out of the blue. I'll just be doing my normal routine, and then it starts. So, no, I haven't noticed anything specific that sets it off.
Have you experienced any major stressful events or trauma in your life — things like abuse, accidents, loss of someone close to you, or other really difficult experiences?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't been through anything like that. No bad accidents or abuse, and I haven't lost anyone close to me. My life has been pretty... normal, I guess. Just regular everyday stress, but definitely no major trauma or anything really difficult like what you're asking about.

During these episodes when you're stuck or repeating the numbers, does it ever feel like a different part of you or a different person is taking over, or do you always feel like it's just you doing these things?

Um, no, it doesn't feel like that. It's definitely just me. I don't feel like another person or a different part of me is taking over or anything. Like I said before, I know I'm the one saying the numbers and standing there... I just get stuck. But it's always just me doing it.

When you're repeating those table numbers, do you feel like you're choosing to say them, or does it feel like the words are just coming out of your mouth on their own without you deciding to say them?

Um... no, it doesn't really feel like that. I mean, I'm definitely the one choosing to say them. It's not like my mouth is just moving on its own or anything. 

It's more that my brain just gets completely stuck on those specific numbers, and... I just feel like I have to say them out loud. But I'm always the one doing it. I don't feel like the words are just spilling out without me deciding to speak.

Looking back over the past few weeks or months before these episodes started happening, have you noticed any changes in your mood, sleep, or anxiety levels, or has anything been weighing on your mind — even if it doesn't feel directly connected to what's happening at work?

Um, no, I haven't really noticed any changes like that. My mood has been pretty much the same, I think. I sleep okay, just regular amounts. And I don't feel any more anxious than usual. There hasn't really been anything heavy weighing on my mind or anything different going on before all this started. Everything was just... normal.

During one of these episodes when you're stuck repeating the numbers, if someone had grabbed your arm or called your name loudly, do you think you would have been able to snap out of it and respond to them, or would you have been completely unable to stop what you were doing?

Um... I'm actually not sure. Nobody has ever really tried to grab my arm or yell my name when it happens. Usually, people just kind of look at me or walk away. So... I don't really know if I would snap out of it or if I'd still be stuck. I just haven't had that happen to say for sure.

When you're repeating those table numbers, does your body do anything unusual at the same time — like your arms or hands moving in a way you're not controlling, or your face twitching, or anything like that?

Um, no, not that I've noticed. I don't think my body does anything weird. My hands aren't moving on their own or anything like that, and my face isn't twitching. It's really just... the numbers. I'm just standing there saying the numbers. I haven't felt my body doing anything out of my control.

When you're repeating those table numbers, does it feel like something you're doing because you feel you have to, or does it feel more like your voice or mouth is acting on its own without your control?

Um, I don't think it's really either of those. It doesn't feel like something I have to do, like a rule or anything. And my mouth isn't moving on its own... I know I'm the one talking. It's just... the numbers just come out. I don't really know how else to explain it, but it doesn't feel like I've lost control of my voice, it just happens.
When you start repeating the table numbers, is that something you decide to do on purpose, or does it just start happening without you making a conscious choice to begin it?

I definitely don't decide to do it on purpose. It just sort of starts happening. I think that's what scared everyone at work, honestly. I would just start freezing up right in the middle of service, or I'd do things totally out of order. Like... I'd end up standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I'd just be repeating the table numbers instead of actually closing out the checks. So, no, I'm not making a conscious choice to begin doing it, it just happens.

When you're standing there repeating the table numbers, do you feel like you could stop yourself and say something different right now if you really tried, or does it feel impossible to stop once it's started?

Um, well, like I was just saying a second ago... when I get stuck like that, freezing up by the soda station with the cash drawer key, I don't really try to stop. I'm just completely out of order. I'm standing there repeating the numbers instead of closing out the checks, and it's not exactly that it feels impossible to stop, it's more like... I'm just frozen in it. I don't even realize I should stop and do something different until someone snaps me out of it.

When you're repeating those table numbers, do you feel like you're doing it because your brain is stuck on those numbers and you're choosing to say them, or does it feel more automatic and repetitive — like something your body just does over and over without you really thinking about it?

Yeah, it's definitely more automatic. Like I was just saying, I'm not really thinking about it or choosing to say them. 

I think that automatic part is exactly why it scared everyone at work so much. I wasn't thinking, I would just start freezing up right in the middle of service and doing things completely out of order. You know, like I mentioned before, I'd just be standing over by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and those table numbers are just coming out over and over on their own, instead of me actually closing out the checks like I was supposed to be doing.

When you're standing there repeating those table numbers over and over, if you tried really hard right in that moment, do you think you could force yourself to say something completely different instead, like a customer's name or something else, or does it feel like only those numbers can come out?

I really don't think I could force myself to say a customer's name or anything else. Honestly, like I keep mentioning, I'm just totally frozen when it happens. 

That's exactly what scared everyone at work so much—I'd just freeze up right in the middle of service and do everything out of order. I'm just stuck standing by the soda station with that cash drawer key, and only the table numbers come out. I wouldn't be able to just switch words because I'm completely stuck doing that instead of closing out the checks.

I'm just frozen in it. I don't even realize I should stop and do something different until someone snaps me out of it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient experiences involuntary repetitive movements or vocalizations (motor or vocal tics) that would suggest Tourette's disorder, or whether the episodes are purely behavioral/cognitive in nature consistent with dissociative or conversion disorder
doctor.question: When you're repeating those table numbers, do you feel like you're doing it because your brain is stuck on those numbers and you're choosing to say them, or does it feel more automatic and repetitive — like something your body just does over and over without you really thinking about it?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: What scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service or doing things out of order, like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for further clarification about the nature of the patient's behavior (repeating table numbers), specifically whether it feels like a conscious choice or an automatic, repetitive action. This relates directly to the disorganized/abnormal behavior symptom (S022).

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's definitely more automatic. Like I was just saying, I'm not really thinking about it or choosing to say them. 

I think that automatic part is exactly why it scared everyone at work so much. I wasn't thinking, I would just start freezing up right in the middle of service and doing things completely out of order. You know, like I mentioned before, I'd just be standing over by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and those table numbers are just coming out over and over on their own, instead of me actually closing out the checks like I was supposed to be doing.

inference.note: Ruled out F44.81 (dissociative identity disorder). Patient denies feeling like a different person/part is taking over, denies loss of consciousness, and denies complete amnesia for episodes. The automatic repetitive behavior, lack of conscious choice to start, freezing in place, and inability to shift attention fit better with F44.4 (conversion disorder with seizures and convulsions) or specific dissociative motor symptoms rather than DID. The involuntary, automatic quality of the repetitive speech and motor freezing, combined with preserved awareness but inability to redirect attention, is most consistent with F44.4.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behavior (saying table numbers) involves involuntary vocalization/palilalia or is a purposeful but automatic motor/behavioral sequence, to help differentiate Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder with dissociative features from other possibilities like Stereotypic Movement Disorder or OCD-spectrum presentations.
doctor.question: When you're standing there repeating those table numbers over and over, if you tried really hard right in that moment, do you think you could force yourself to say something completely different instead, like a customer's name or something else, or does it feel like only those numbers can come out?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: What scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service or doing things out of order, like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking for further clarification about the patient's behavior of repeating table numbers while frozen, which is a manifestation of disorganized/abnormal behavior (S022).

patient.answer:
I really don't think I could force myself to say a customer's name or anything else. Honestly, like I keep mentioning, I'm just totally frozen when it happens. 

That's exactly what scared everyone at work so much—I'd just freeze up right in the middle of service and do everything out of order. I'm just stuck standing by the soda station with that cash drawer key, and only the table numbers come out. I wouldn't be able to just switch words because I'm completely stuck doing that instead of closing out the checks.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with recurrent episodes of involuntary repetitive vocalizations (repeating table numbers) and behavioral freezing that occur without conscious intent, accompanied by apparent lack of awareness of surroundings during episodes, but with preserved consciousness and no loss of awareness of self. The symptoms are automatic, not consciously controlled, and cannot be voluntarily stopped once initiated. There is no identified traumatic stressor, no dissociative amnesia, no motor or sensory deficits, and no evidence of neurological or medical causation. The presentation is most consistent with F44.4 (Conversion disorder with motor symptom or deficit), specifically the motor/behavioral manifestation variant, though the vocalization component and automatic nature also warrant consideration of F44.5 (Conversion disorder with seizures or convulsions) and F98.8 (Other specified behavioral and emotional disorders of childhood and adolescence) as differential considerations.
